questions.question: Choose the correct form: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ available yesterday.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb commonly agrees with the nearer subject, 'teachers'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Each of the participants ___ given a certificate.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: The bouquet of roses ___ lovely.
questions.explanation: The head of the subject is the singular noun 'bouquet'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk in this heat.
questions.explanation: A distance considered as one unit takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: The jury ___ reached its decision.
questions.explanation: Here the jury is treated as one collective body.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: She ___ the assignment before the deadline yesterday.
questions.explanation: The simple past is used for a completed action at a stated past time.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: I ___ for you for an hour when you finally arrived.
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous emphasizes an ongoing action before a later past event.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: By next June, he ___ here for five years.
questions.explanation: Future perfect expresses completion by a specified future time.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: If I ___ about the change, I would have attended.
questions.explanation: The third conditional uses past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Unless you ___ regularly, you may lose confidence.
questions.explanation: After 'unless' referring to the future, the present simple is normally used.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: I would rather you ___ the matter confidential.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' followed by a different subject commonly takes a past form for a present preference.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: It is essential that every applicant ___ the form.
questions.explanation: The mandative subjunctive uses the base form after 'it is essential that'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The proposal ___ by the committee tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The future passive emphasizes the proposal receiving the action.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The room ___ when we entered.
questions.explanation: The past continuous passive shows an action in progress at that past moment.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The teacher asked us ___ our phones away.
questions.explanation: 'Ask + object + to-infinitive' is used for reported requests or instructions.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: He denied ___ the window.
questions.explanation: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund when referring to an action.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She managed ___ the difficult problem.
questions.explanation: 'Manage' is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: I remember ___ him at the conference last year.
questions.explanation: 'Remember doing' refers to recalling a past experience.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Remember ___ the door before you leave.
questions.explanation: 'Remember to do' means not forget a task that needs to be done.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The students were encouraged ___ questions.
questions.explanation: 'Encourage + object + to-infinitive' is the correct pattern.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: She gave me ___ useful piece of advice.
questions.explanation: 'Useful' begins with a /juː/ consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: We visited ___ Netherlands during the summer.
questions.explanation: Some country names, including 'the Netherlands', take the definite article.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: He hopes to become ___ engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, requiring 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She has been waiting ___ 9 a.m.
questions.explanation: 'Since' introduces the starting point of a period.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: We have lived here ___ six months.
questions.explanation: 'For' introduces the duration of time.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The cat jumped ___ the wall and disappeared.
questions.explanation: 'Over' indicates movement across and above the wall.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The teacher distributed the worksheets ___ the learners.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for distribution involving more than two people.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The agreement was signed ___ both parties.
questions.explanation: In a passive sentence, 'by' introduces the agent.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She is responsible ___ organizing the event.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'responsible' is followed by 'for'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: He succeeded ___ convincing the panel.
questions.explanation: 'Succeed in' is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The teacher objected ___ the use of offensive language.
questions.explanation: 'Object to' is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The school decided to ___ a new reading programme.
questions.explanation: 'Set up' means establish or start.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: Please ___ the main points in your own words.
questions.explanation: 'Sum up' means summarize.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The fire ___ before the firefighters arrived.
questions.explanation: 'Break out' means begin suddenly, especially of a fire or conflict.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: I cannot ___ what the sign says from here.
questions.explanation: 'Make out' can mean discern or understand.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: She ___ an interesting point during the discussion.
questions.explanation: 'Bring up' means introduce a topic for discussion.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The school will ___ a new policy next term.
questions.explanation: 'Adopt' means formally accept or begin to use.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: Learners need to ___ to changing classroom demands.
questions.explanation: 'Adapt' means adjust to new conditions.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The speaker's argument was ___ by relevant examples.
questions.explanation: 'Supported by examples' is the appropriate collocation.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The instructions were so ___ that pupils could follow them independently.
questions.explanation: 'Comprehensible' means easy to understand.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: A ___ reader considers the reliability of a source.
questions.explanation: 'Critical' is the adjective describing careful evaluation.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'innovative'.
questions.explanation: 'Innovative' means introducing new ideas or methods.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'feasible'.
questions.explanation: 'Feasible' means capable of being done successfully.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'obtain'.
questions.explanation: 'Obtain' means get or acquire.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'interpret'.
questions.explanation: 'Interpret' means explain or understand the meaning of something.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'proficient'.
questions.explanation: 'Proficient' means competent or skilled.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'explicit'.
questions.explanation: 'Implicit' means suggested rather than directly stated.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'optimise'.
questions.explanation: 'Worsen' contrasts with optimise, which means make as effective as possible.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'mandatory'.
questions.explanation: 'Optional' means not compulsory.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'genuine'.
questions.explanation: 'Counterfeit' means fake, the opposite of genuine.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'consecutive'.
questions.explanation: 'Intermittent' means occurring at intervals rather than continuously or in succession.

questions.question: What does 'burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: Work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: The idiom means work or study late at night.

questions.question: What does 'beat around the bush' mean?
options: Avoid addressing the main point directly
questions.explanation: The idiom means avoid saying something directly.

questions.question: What does 'the ball is in your court' mean?
options: It is your turn or responsibility to act
questions.explanation: The expression means the next action or decision is yours.

questions.question: What does 'call it a day' mean?
options: Stop working for the time being
Name the days of the week
questions.explanation: The idiom means stop an activity, especially work.

questions.question: What does 'in a nutshell' mean?
options: In a brief and concise form
questions.explanation: The expression introduces a brief summary.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: After the lesson, we reviewed the answers.
After the lesson we, reviewed the answers.
After, the lesson we reviewed the answers.
After the lesson we reviewed, the answers.
questions.explanation: The introductory phrase is appropriately followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: The comma introduces the direct quotation, and the final punctuation is placed inside the closing quotation mark in this style.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: Bring these items: a pencil, an eraser and a ruler.
Bring: these items a pencil, an eraser and a ruler.
Bring these: items a pencil, an eraser and a ruler.
Bring these items a pencil: an eraser and a ruler.
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete clause.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a hyphen correctly?
options: She is a well known author in all cases.
questions.explanation: A hyphen commonly joins words in a compound modifier before a noun.

questions.question: Which sentence is free from a misplaced modifier?
options: She almost drove her children to school every day.
She drove her children to school almost every day.
Almost she drove her children to school every day.
She drove almost her children to school every day.
questions.explanation: The placement of 'almost' clearly modifies the frequency of driving.

questions.question: Which is a compound-complex sentence?
options: Although it was raining, we continued, and the coach encouraged us.
It was raining, and we continued.
Although it was raining, we continued.
questions.explanation: It contains a subordinate clause and two independent clauses.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an appositive?
options: My friend, a skilled violinist, performed tonight.
My friend performed tonight because she practised.
My friend who performed tonight is skilled.
My friend performed and then left.
questions.explanation: 'A skilled violinist' renames and identifies 'my friend'.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a noun phrase functioning as the subject?
questions.explanation: 'The old wooden bridge' is a noun phrase functioning as the subject.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an adverbial phrase of manner?
options: The child with confidence was selected.
The child gave a confident answer.
questions.explanation: 'With confidence' describes how the child answered.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a comparative adjective?
options: This passage is more challenging than the previous one.
This passage is most challenging than the previous one.
This passage is challenginger than the previous one.
This passage is more challenging as the previous one.
questions.explanation: 'More challenging than' is the correct comparative construction.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: This is the ___ of the two proposals.
questions.explanation: For comparing two items, 'better' is the appropriate comparative form.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: Of all the speakers, Mira spoke ___.
questions.explanation: The superlative adverb 'most clearly' compares Mira with all speakers.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: You may borrow the book ___ you return it by Friday.
questions.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a condition.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: ___ he was nervous, he delivered the speech confidently.
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a contrast between nervousness and confident delivery.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: The task was difficult; ___, the learners completed it.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' signals contrast.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: The bus was delayed; ___, we arrived after the bell.
questions.explanation: 'Consequently' signals a result.

questions.question: Which option is the clearest paraphrase of 'Learners benefit when feedback is timely and specific'?
options: Feedback helps learners when it arrives promptly and identifies particular improvements.
Learners dislike all feedback that is specific.
Feedback should be delayed and general.
questions.explanation: The paraphrase preserves the ideas of promptness and specificity.

questions.question: Which sentence best summarizes a passage explaining several causes of water pollution?
options: Water pollution results from multiple sources, including waste discharge, runoff and litter.
The passage mentions a river on page two.
questions.explanation: A summary captures the central idea and main supporting categories.

questions.question: Which question asks for an inference?
options: What can be concluded from the character's actions and the details given?
Where does the story take place, as stated in paragraph one?
How many lines are in the poem?
questions.explanation: Inference requires drawing a conclusion from clues rather than retrieving an explicit fact.

questions.question: Which task best assesses a reader's ability to identify a claim?
options: Underline the statement the author is trying to establish as true
questions.explanation: Identifying a claim means locating the central assertion being advanced.

questions.question: Which is the most useful first step when approaching an unfamiliar informational text?
options: Preview the title, headings and visuals to anticipate its topic and structure
Read only the final word of each paragraph
questions.explanation: Previewing text features activates expectations and gives an initial map of the text.

questions.question: Which activity practises scanning?
options: Locate the date and venue in an event notice
Evaluate the strength of an argument
questions.explanation: Scanning searches quickly for particular pieces of information.

questions.question: Which activity practises skimming?
options: Read headings and topic sentences to identify the main idea
Search for a particular phone number
Check the spelling of one word
questions.explanation: Skimming is rapid reading for the general meaning.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate strategy for teaching a poem's imagery?
options: Ask learners to identify sensory details and explain the effects they create
Require learners to memorize the poet's biography only
Translate every word without discussing meaning
questions.explanation: Exploring sensory details connects language choices to their effects on readers.

questions.question: Which activity best develops listening for sequence?
options: Arrange event cards in the order described in the recording
Count the number of speakers without following content
questions.explanation: Sequencing cards checks whether learners understand the order of events.

questions.question: Which activity best develops listening for attitude?
options: Compare word choice and vocal cues to decide whether the speaker sounds doubtful or enthusiastic
Record the length of the audio file
Copy the title of the recording
Identify every noun without considering context
questions.explanation: Attitude can be inferred from the speaker's words, tone and delivery.

questions.question: Which classroom activity is a genuine information-gap task?
options: Each partner has different timetable details and asks questions to complete a shared schedule
Both partners copy the same completed timetable
One learner reads while the other remains silent
The teacher gives every answer before pair work
questions.explanation: An information gap requires partners to exchange information unavailable to each other.

questions.question: Which response best encourages a learner to extend a spoken answer?
options: Could you give an example to support that idea?
questions.explanation: A request for an example invites elaboration and supporting detail.

questions.question: Which is an effective way to teach turn-taking in discussion?
options: Model polite entry phrases and practise responding to a partner's contribution
Allow only one learner to speak throughout
questions.explanation: Explicit modelling and practice make interaction conventions visible.

questions.question: Which task best practises writing a persuasive paragraph?
options: State a position, support it with reasons and evidence, and address a counterpoint
List unrelated facts without a claim
Write a dialogue with no stated purpose
questions.explanation: Persuasive writing develops a position through reasons and evidence.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate feature of a narrative opening?
options: Introduce a setting or situation that gives readers a point of entry
questions.explanation: A narrative opening establishes context for the events that follow.

questions.question: Which task best develops process writing?
options: Plan, draft, receive feedback, revise and edit a piece of writing
Submit the first sentence as the final draft
Memorize a model essay without writing
questions.explanation: Process writing treats composition as a sequence of planning, drafting and revision stages.

questions.question: Which feedback is most useful for improving paragraph coherence?
options: Reorder these two sentences so the supporting idea follows the topic sentence.
Write the paragraph again without guidance.
questions.explanation: The comment identifies a specific change connected to logical organization.

questions.question: Which practice supports vocabulary retention?
options: Revisit new words in varied contexts and encourage learners to use them
Present each word once and never return to it
Teach spelling without meaning or context
Ask learners to copy a list without retrieval
questions.explanation: Repeated encounters and meaningful use support long-term retention.

questions.question: Which approach helps learners notice collocations?
options: Compare examples such as 'make a decision' and 'do homework' in context
Teach words only in alphabetical order
Avoid examples of words used together
Replace every phrase with a single isolated word
questions.explanation: Collocation teaching highlights words that commonly occur together.

questions.question: Which classroom activity promotes learner autonomy?
options: Learners select a suitable reading strategy, explain their choice and evaluate its usefulness
The teacher chooses every strategy and forbids reflection
Learners wait for the teacher to solve each difficulty
Learners are graded on speed alone
questions.explanation: Choosing and evaluating strategies gives learners responsibility for their learning.

questions.question: Which is an example of formative assessment in a language lesson?
options: The teacher uses responses during pair work to decide what to clarify next
A final certificate issued at course completion
A year-end ranking used for promotion
A report card with no feedback during the course
questions.explanation: Formative assessment informs teaching and learning while the course is in progress.

questions.question: Which is an example of summative assessment?
options: A final speaking examination used to report achievement at the end of a course
A quick oral check used to adjust today's lesson
Peer feedback on an early draft
questions.explanation: Summative assessment reports achievement at the end of a learning period.

questions.question: Which quality refers to consistency of assessment results?
questions.explanation: Reliability concerns the consistency of scores or judgments.

questions.question: Which quality concerns whether a test measures what it intends to measure?
questions.explanation: Validity concerns the appropriateness of the interpretation and use of assessment evidence.

questions.question: Which task has strong communicative authenticity?
options: Write an email requesting information that the learner genuinely needs
Fill a page with disconnected verb forms
Copy a dialogue without reading it
questions.explanation: The task resembles purposeful language use outside a test-only setting.

questions.question: Which accommodation may support a learner with a visual difficulty?
options: Provide accessible large-print or digital text as appropriate
Remove the learner from all reading tasks
Use smaller print to save space
Assess only through copying from the board
questions.explanation: Accessible text formats can reduce visual barriers while preserving the learning objective.

questions.question: Which teaching practice supports multilingual learners?
options: Connect new English vocabulary to known concepts and provide visual or contextual scaffolds
Assume home-language knowledge prevents English learning
Use unfamiliar idioms in every instruction
questions.explanation: Connecting to existing knowledge and adding scaffolds can aid access to English learning.

questions.question: Which teacher response is most constructive when a learner makes an error?
options: Invite the learner to reconsider with a prompt and acknowledge useful parts of the response
Make the error a subject of ridicule
questions.explanation: Guided, respectful feedback treats errors as opportunities for learning.
